scenarios.name: Baseline policy
scenarios.description: Starting stock: Ingredient A as three lots with different remaining lives (90, 140 and 156 weeks), Ingredient B as one lot, and 4,300 units of finished Product expiring in 28 weeks. Demand starts at its mean, 4.5 orders per week.

scenarios.name: Calm market (no noise)
scenarios.description: Demand and price volatility set to 0, so the SDEs become ODEs and both relax deterministically to their means. Everything else matches the baseline.

scenarios.name: Volatile market (demand volatility × 3)
scenarios.description: Demand volatility 3.9, three times the default: spikes and droughts. The scenario that motivates holding stock at all.

scenarios.name: Demand surge (transient)
scenarios.description: Demand starts at three times its mean (13.5 orders per week) and mean-reverts. Tests whether the purchasing policy survives a spike.

scenarios.name: Fragile supply (outage rate × 5)
scenarios.description: Suppliers run out of stock at 0.2 per week (~10 outages a year each, ~2-week mean outage: out of stock ~29% of the time). The scenario that gives dual sourcing and the switch mechanism their job, and exposes Ingredient A's single sourcing, which has no substitute.

scenarios.name: Depleted start (initial stock is 0)
scenarios.description: No stock anywhere, demand at its mean. Everything must be bought, made and sold within the horizon.

scenarios.name: Shipment delays (delay rate × 10)
scenarios.description: Shipments hit holds at 0.2 per week per open order (~1 in 3 orders on the slow Supplier A leg). The stress case for the delayed-shipment mechanism, as Fragile supply is for outages: material ages in the hold and arrives late or expired.

scenarios.name: Volatile prices (price volatility × 4)
scenarios.description: The raw-material price index swings hard (typical excursions ~25%) while demand keeps its default volatility. The same purchasing policy now produces a different bill every run, a gap a price-aware policy could close.

scenarios.name: Recall wave (recall hazard armed)
scenarios.description: Every stored lot carries a 0.02 per week recall hazard: whole lots leave the shelves for RecalledStock with disposal costs, and the reorder-point policy has to re-buy through the quarantine pipeline. A stress scenario by design.

scenarios.name: Optimise policy
scenarios.description: The baseline with the purchasing policy exposed for optimisation: reorder point and order-up-to target per ingredient, the Supplier C top-up threshold and quantity, and the production forecast weight (0 = fixed plan batches, 1 = make-to-forecast). Defaults reproduce the baseline policy. Keep each target at or above its reorder point; minimise Policy cost (EUR) and monitor Fill rate, ending backlog, production queue and expiry.

metrics.name: Demand rate now (orders per week)
metrics.description: The OU-evolving arrival rate lambda(t). Its mean is demand_mu; excursions are the SDE at work.

metrics.name: Backlog (orders waiting)
metrics.description: Customer orders received and not yet fulfilled or cancelled.

metrics.name: Orders fulfilled
metrics.description: Sales completed within the horizon.

metrics.name: Sum of fulfilment lead times (weeks)
metrics.description: Sum of `waited` at fulfilment. Average lead time = this / orders fulfilled.

metrics.name: Lost sales (spot orders cancelled)
metrics.description: Spot orders cancelled (count). Units lost is the companion metric.

metrics.name: Raw stock on shelf, Ingredient A (units)
metrics.description: Sum of stock qty on the shelf.

metrics.name: Raw stock on shelf, Ingredient B (units)
metrics.description: Sum of stock qty on the shelf.

metrics.name: Stock in transit (units)
metrics.description: Sum of stock qty in transit, all vendors.

metrics.name: Finished goods, Product (units)
metrics.description: Sum of stock qty in the finished store.

metrics.name: Expired stock written off (units)
metrics.description: Quantity lost to shelf-life expiry, raw and finished.

metrics.name: Batches scrapped (QC)
metrics.description: Batches lost to QC failure in production.

metrics.name: Purchase orders placed
metrics.description: All suppliers.

metrics.name: Purchase spend (EUR)
metrics.description: Committed on placed orders at the price captured at order time (base unit prices scaled by the price index). Switching fees are a separate metric.

metrics.name: Supplier switches (substitute orders)
metrics.description: Ingredient B orders redirected to Supplier C while Supplier B was out of stock.

metrics.name: Shipments lost in transit
metrics.description: Consignments lost in transit. The supplier reships a replacement (fresh dispatch leg, mean transit leg, full shelf life), so a loss costs lead time, not money; the replacement keeps the order-time price.

metrics.name: Reshipped consignment value (EUR)
metrics.description: Value of consignments lost and reshipped, at the order-time price. Not a write-off: the vendor honours the order, so the cost of a loss is the extra lead time, not the money.

metrics.name: Switching fees (EUR)
metrics.description: Cost of redirecting orders (switch_cost per substitute order). Total purchasing cost = spend + this.

metrics.name: Ingredient A in transit (units)
metrics.description: Ingredient A units shipped and not yet received.

metrics.name: Orders fulfilled (contract)
metrics.description: Split of fulfilled orders by segment colour.

metrics.name: Contract tardiness (order-weeks)
metrics.description: Sum over fulfilled contract orders of max(0, waited - delivery window). Demand is conserved for contracts; lateness costs money instead of orders.

metrics.name: Late-delivery penalties (EUR)
metrics.description: Contract tardiness priced at late_penalty_per_week. Composes with purchase spend and switching fees into one cost objective.

metrics.name: Shipments delayed (cumulative)
metrics.description: Shipments that hit a customs or goods-receipt hold. The stock keeps ageing while held and is released on a slower timescale; held stock cannot be lost (losses apply only in transit).

metrics.name: Units held up in delayed shipments
metrics.description: Current qty sitting in the hold, still ageing.

metrics.name: Raw material price index (now)
metrics.description: The OU-evolving multiplier on the base unit prices. Mean 1.0; excursions are the price SDE at work.

metrics.name: Stock at supplier, not yet shipped (units)
metrics.description: Order book: accepted orders awaiting dispatch. A supplier outage stalls this place, since dispatch needs the supplier's InStock token.

metrics.name: Ingredient A at supplier (units)
metrics.description: Ingredient A units ordered and awaiting dispatch.

metrics.name: Holding costs banked (EUR)
metrics.description: Storage cost accrued by stock that has since been discarded or written off. Total holding cost = this + the three live-accrual metrics.

metrics.name: Holding cost accrued, Ingredient A shelf (EUR)
metrics.description: Live accrual on stock currently stored.

metrics.name: Holding cost accrued, Ingredient B shelf (EUR)
metrics.description: Live accrual on stock currently stored.

metrics.name: Holding cost accrued, Product store (EUR)
metrics.description: Live accrual on stock currently stored.

metrics.name: Units sold
metrics.description: Sum of fulfilled order quantities.

metrics.name: Units lost (spot cancellations)
metrics.description: Demand that walked away, in units.

metrics.name: Backlog (units waiting)
metrics.description: Open demand in units. Order qty is clamped >= 5 once, at arrival, so this reads it raw.

metrics.name: Scheduled batches waiting
metrics.description: Planned production orders not yet started; rises when materials starve the plan.

metrics.name: Inventory position, Ingredient A (units)
metrics.description: on-hand + at-vendor + in-transit − committed; quarantined/rejected/recalled/expired excluded. The reorder-point policy's decision variable.

metrics.name: Inventory position, Ingredient B (units)
metrics.description: As the Ingredient A position.

metrics.name: Stock in quarantine (units)
metrics.description: Delivered but not yet quality-released — unavailable to production and excluded from the inventory position.

metrics.name: QC-rejected stock (units)
metrics.description: Receipts that failed inspection (assumed ~5%).

metrics.name: Recalled stock (units)
metrics.description: Stock pulled by recall events (Recall wave scenario).

metrics.name: Disposal costs (EUR)
metrics.description: Controlled destruction and admin on expiry, QC rejection and recalls, at disposal_cost per unit. Excludes purchase spend and holding already counted elsewhere.

metrics.name: Lost margin, cancelled spot (EUR)
metrics.description: Lost units × contribution margin (unit_margin).

metrics.name: Production delay cost, banked (EUR)
metrics.description: waited x qty x rate charged when a late scheduled batch finally starts.

metrics.name: Production delay cost, accruing (EUR)
metrics.description: The same charge accruing on batches still waiting for materials. Total shortage cost = banked + this.
metrics.code: return state.places["ProductionOrdersWaiting"].tokens.reduce((n, t) => n + t.waited * t.produce_qty * parameters.shortage_cost_rate, 0);

metrics.name: Policy cost (EUR)
metrics.description: The single objective for optimisation: purchase spend + holding (banked and still accruing on live stock, quarantine included) + lost margin on cancelled spot orders + production delay (banked and accruing) + late-delivery penalties + switching fees + disposal. Equals the sum of the component metrics by construction.
metrics.code: return state.places["OrdersPlaced"].tokens.reduce((n, t) => n + t.qty * t.unit_price, state.places["HoldingCosts"].tokens.concat(state.places["SwitchFees"].tokens).concat(state.places["DisposalCosts"].tokens).concat(state.places["ShortageCosts"].tokens).reduce((m, t) => m + t.value, state.places["LostSales"].tokens.reduce((l, t) => l + t.value * parameters.unit_margin, state.places["FulfilledOrders"].tokens.reduce((f, t) => f + t.tardiness * parameters.late_penalty_per_week, state.places["ProductionOrdersWaiting"].tokens.reduce((s, t) => s + t.waited * t.produce_qty * parameters.shortage_cost_rate, state.places["IngredientAStock"].tokens.concat(state.places["IngredientBStock"].tokens).concat(state.places["FinishedGoods"].tokens).concat(state.places["Quarantine"].tokens).reduce((h, c) => h + c.holding_eur, 0))))));

metrics.name: Fill rate (sold / demanded units)
metrics.description: Units sold over all demanded units (sold + cancelled + still in the backlog), so a policy cannot look cheap by under-buying and failing customers. The 0.001 seed guards the division at t = 0.
metrics.code: return state.places["DemandOutlook"].tokens.reduce((ratio, d) => state.places["FulfilledOrders"].tokens.reduce((s, t) => s + t.qty, 0) / ratio, state.places["FulfilledOrders"].tokens.reduce((a, t) => a + t.qty, state.places["LostSales"].tokens.reduce((b, t) => b + t.value, state.places["Backlog"].tokens.reduce((c, t) => c + t.qty, 0.001))));

title: Inventory Purchasing
description: A manufacturer buys two ingredients, makes one product from them, and sells it to contract and spot customers. Ingredient A is single-sourced from Supplier A on a slow transit leg; Ingredient B is bought from Supplier B, topped up from Supplier C when stock runs low, and switched to Supplier C (for a fee) while Supplier B is out of stock. Purchasing follows a reorder-point, order-up-to policy on each ingredient's inventory position, subject to minimum order quantities and rounding. Demand and the raw-material price index follow Ornstein–Uhlenbeck processes. Stock carries its shelf life through order, transit, customs holds, quality quarantine, production and the finished-goods store, accruing holding cost on the shelf and risking loss, rejection, recall and expiry. Policy cost composes spend, holding, lost margin, production delay, late penalties, switching fees and disposal into one objective, with Fill rate as the service-level check; the Optimise policy scenario exposes the purchasing parameters for search.
